```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmnet)
library(rsample)
library(randomForest)
library(xgboost)
library(yardstick)
library(ggplot2)
library(shapviz)
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD DATA & VARIABLE GROUPS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
data <- read.csv("hpi_clean_full.csv")
```

```{r}
set.seed(42)

# 80/20 train-test split (stratified by income_quartile)
split <- initial_split(data, prop = 0.80, strata = income_quartile)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data <- testing(split)

cat("Training rows:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Test rows:    ", nrow(test_data), "\n")
```

```{r}
var_groups <- readRDS("variable_groups.rds")
indicators_raw <- var_groups$indicators_raw
domain_scores <- var_groups$domain_scores
demo_vars <- var_groups$demo_vars
response_var <- var_groups$response_var

# Re-apply factor levels lost during CSV write
train_data <- train_data %>%
  mutate(
    income_quartile = factor(income_quartile,
                             levels = c("Q1_low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4_high")),
    hpi_quartile = factor(hpi_quartile),
    urban_type = factor(urban_type)
  )
 
test_data <- test_data %>%
  mutate(
    income_quartile = factor(income_quartile,
                             levels = c("Q1_low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4_high")),
    hpi_quartile    = factor(hpi_quartile),
    urban_type      = factor(urban_type)
  )
 
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. CREATE REGION VARIABLE FROM COUNTIES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
bay_area <- c(
  "Alameda", "Contra Costa", "Marin", "Napa", "San Francisco",
  "San Mateo", "Santa Clara", "Solano", "Sonoma"
)
socal <- c(
  "Los Angeles", "Orange", "Riverside", "San Bernardino",
  "San Diego", "Imperial", "Ventura"
)
central_valley <- c(
  "Fresno", "Kern", "Kings", "Madera", "Merced",
  "San Joaquin", "Stanislaus", "Tulare"
)
norcal <- c(
  "Butte", "Colusa", "Del Norte", "Glenn", "Humboldt", "Lake",
  "Lassen", "Mendocino", "Modoc", "Plumas", "Shasta", "Sierra",
  "Siskiyou", "Tehama", "Trinity"
)
 
assign_region <- function(county_name) {
  case_when(
    county_name %in% bay_area       ~ "Bay Area",
    county_name %in% socal          ~ "SoCal",
    county_name %in% central_valley ~ "Central Valley",
    county_name %in% norcal         ~ "NorCal",
    TRUE                            ~ "Other CA"
  )
}
 
train_data <- train_data %>%
  mutate(region = factor(assign_region(county)))
 
test_data <- test_data %>%
  mutate(region = factor(assign_region(county)))
 
final_df <- final_df %>%
  mutate(region = factor(assign_region(county)))
 
cat("Region distribution in training data:\n")
print(table(train_data$region))
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. LASSO — VARIABLE SELECTION
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
lasso_vars <- c(indicators_raw, demo_vars)
 
x_train <- train_data %>%
  select(all_of(lasso_vars)) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  as.matrix()
 
y_train <- train_data %>%
  filter(complete.cases(select(., all_of(lasso_vars)))) %>%
  pull(leb_cdc)
 
x_test <- test_data %>%
  select(all_of(lasso_vars)) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  as.matrix()
 
y_test <- test_data %>%
  filter(complete.cases(select(., all_of(lasso_vars)))) %>%
  pull(leb_cdc)
 
# Cross-validated LASSO to find optimal lambda
set.seed(42)
lasso_cv <- cv.glmnet(
  x         = x_train,
  y         = y_train,
  alpha     = 1,          # alpha=1 is LASSO (alpha=0 is Ridge)
  nfolds    = 10,
  standardize = TRUE      # standardize predictors (important for LASSO)
)
 
plot(lasso_cv)
title("LASSO Cross-Validation — Lambda Selection", line = 3)
 
# Best lambda (1 SE rule — more parsimonious model)
best_lambda <- lasso_cv$lambda.1se
cat("\nBest lambda (1SE):", round(best_lambda, 4), "\n")
 
# Extract non-zero coefficients = selected variables
lasso_coefs <- coef(lasso_cv, s = "lambda.1se")
selected_vars <- rownames(lasso_coefs)[which(lasso_coefs != 0)]
selected_vars <- selected_vars[selected_vars != "(Intercept)"]
 
cat("\nLASSO selected", length(selected_vars), "variables:\n")
print(selected_vars)
 
# LASSO predictions on test set
lasso_preds <- predict(lasso_cv, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.1se") %>% as.vector()
 
lasso_rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_test - lasso_preds)^2))
lasso_r2   <- cor(y_test, lasso_preds)^2
cat("\nLASSO Test RMSE:", round(lasso_rmse, 3))
cat("\nLASSO Test R²:  ", round(lasso_r2, 3), "\n")
 
# Coefficient plot — shows direction and magnitude of selected predictors
lasso_coef_df <- data.frame(
  variable    = selected_vars,
  coefficient = as.vector(lasso_coefs[selected_vars, ])
) %>% arrange(coefficient)
 
ggplot(lasso_coef_df, aes(x = reorder(variable, coefficient), y = coefficient)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "LASSO Selected Predictors of Life Expectancy",
       x = NULL, y = "Coefficient") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. 2-WAY ANOVA — REGION x INCOME LEVEL
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
anova_df <- final_df %>%
  select(leb_cdc, region, income_quartile) %>%
  drop_na()
 
# Check cell counts (need reasonable n per cell)
cat("\nCell counts (region x income_quartile):\n")
print(table(anova_df$region, anova_df$income_quartile))
 
# Fit 2-way ANOVA with interaction
anova_model <- aov(leb_cdc ~ region * income_quartile, data = anova_df)
cat("\n2-Way ANOVA Results:\n")
print(summary(anova_model))
 
# Post-hoc: Tukey HSD to see which pairs differ significantly
tukey_results <- TukeyHSD(anova_model)
cat("\nTukey HSD — Region:\n")
print(tukey_results$region)
cat("\nTukey HSD — Income Quartile:\n")
print(tukey_results$income_quartile)
 
# Interaction plot — visualize how income effect varies by region
anova_df %>%
  group_by(region, income_quartile) %>%
  summarise(mean_leb = mean(leb_cdc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = income_quartile, y = mean_leb,
             color = region, group = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Mean Life Expectancy by Region and Income Quartile",
       x = "Income Quartile", y = "Mean Life Expectancy (years)",
       color = "Region") +
  theme_minimal()
 
# Check ANOVA assumptions
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(anova_model)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. K-MEANS CLUSTERING
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
# Use LASSO-selected variables for clustering
cluster_vars <- intersect(selected_vars, colnames(train_data))
 
cluster_df <- final_df %>%
  select(geo_id, all_of(cluster_vars)) %>%
  drop_na()
 
# Scale variables (k-means is distance-based, scaling is required)
cluster_scaled <- cluster_df %>%
  select(-geo_id) %>%
  scale()
 
# Elbow plot — find optimal number of clusters
set.seed(42)
wss <- map_dbl(1:10, ~ {
  kmeans(cluster_scaled, centers = .x, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)$tot.withinss
})
 
tibble(k = 1:10, wss = wss) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = k, y = wss)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(title = "K-Means Elbow Plot",
       x = "Number of Clusters (k)", y = "Total Within-Cluster SS") +
  theme_minimal()
 
# Fit k-means with chosen k (adjust after reviewing elbow plot)
k_chosen <- 4
 
set.seed(42)
kmeans_fit <- kmeans(cluster_scaled, centers = k_chosen,
                     nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
 
# Add cluster labels back to data
cluster_df <- cluster_df %>%
  mutate(cluster = factor(kmeans_fit$cluster))
 
final_df <- final_df %>%
  left_join(cluster_df %>% select(geo_id, cluster), by = "geo_id")
 
cat("\nCluster sizes:\n")
print(table(cluster_df$cluster))
 
# Profile clusters by mean life expectancy
final_df %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    n          = n(),
    mean_leb   = mean(leb_cdc, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_hpi   = mean(hpi, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_income = mean(percapitaincome, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(mean_leb) %>%
  print()
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. RANDOM FOREST
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
# Use LASSO-selected variables as predictors
rf_vars <- selected_vars
 
rf_train <- train_data %>%
  select(all_of(c(rf_vars, "leb_cdc"))) %>%
  drop_na()
 
rf_test <- test_data %>%
  select(all_of(c(rf_vars, "leb_cdc"))) %>%
  drop_na()
 
set.seed(42)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  x        = rf_train %>% select(-leb_cdc),
  y        = rf_train$leb_cdc,
  ntree    = 500,
  mtry     = floor(sqrt(length(rf_vars))),  # default for regression
  importance = TRUE
)
 
print(rf_model)
 
# Variable importance plot
varImpPlot(rf_model, main = "Random Forest — Variable Importance")
 
# Test set predictions
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = rf_test %>% select(-leb_cdc))
 
rf_rmse <- sqrt(mean((rf_test$leb_cdc - rf_preds)^2))
rf_r2   <- cor(rf_test$leb_cdc, rf_preds)^2
cat("\nRandom Forest Test RMSE:", round(rf_rmse, 3))
cat("\nRandom Forest Test R²:  ", round(rf_r2, 3), "\n")
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. XGBOOST
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
# XGBoost requires numeric matrices — factors must be dummy-encoded
xgb_vars <- selected_vars  # already numeric from LASSO step
 
xgb_train_x <- train_data %>%
  select(all_of(xgb_vars)) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  as.matrix()
 
xgb_train_y <- train_data %>%
  filter(complete.cases(select(., all_of(xgb_vars)))) %>%
  pull(leb_cdc)
 
xgb_test_x <- test_data %>%
  select(all_of(xgb_vars)) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  as.matrix()
 
xgb_test_y <- test_data %>%
  filter(complete.cases(select(., all_of(xgb_vars)))) %>%
  pull(leb_cdc)
 
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = xgb_train_x, label = xgb_train_y)
dtest  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = xgb_test_x,  label = xgb_test_y)

params <- list(
  objective     = "reg:squarederror",
  learning_rate = 0.05,
  max_depth     = 4,
  subsample     = 0.8
)

# Cross-validated XGBoost
set.seed(42)
xgb_cv <- xgb.cv(
  data                  = dtrain,
  nrounds               = 500,
  nfold                 = 10,
  params                = params,
  early_stopping_rounds = 20,
  verbose               = 0
)

best_nrounds <- which.min(xgb_cv$evaluation_log$test_rmse_mean)
cat("\nXGBoost best nrounds:", best_nrounds, "\n")

# Fit final XGBoost model
set.seed(42)
xgb_model <- xgb.train(
  data    = dtrain,
  nrounds = best_nrounds,
  params  = params,
  verbose = 0
)
 
# Feature importance
xgb_importance <- xgb.importance(model = xgb_model)
xgb.plot.importance(xgb_importance, top_n = 15,
                    main = "XGBoost — Feature Importance")
 
# Test set predictions
xgb_preds <- predict(xgb_model, dtest)
 
xgb_rmse <- sqrt(mean((xgb_test_y - xgb_preds)^2))
xgb_r2   <- cor(xgb_test_y, xgb_preds)^2
cat("\nXGBoost Test RMSE:", round(xgb_rmse, 3))
cat("\nXGBoost Test R²:  ", round(xgb_r2, 3), "\n")
```

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. MODEL COMPARISON — YOUR MODEL vs HPI BASELINE
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
```{r}
hpi_baseline_df <- test_data %>%
  select(leb_cdc, hpi) %>%
  drop_na()
 
hpi_baseline_model <- lm(leb_cdc ~ hpi, data = hpi_baseline_df)
hpi_baseline_preds <- predict(hpi_baseline_model, hpi_baseline_df)
 
hpi_rmse <- sqrt(mean((hpi_baseline_df$leb_cdc - hpi_baseline_preds)^2))
hpi_r2   <- cor(hpi_baseline_df$leb_cdc, hpi_baseline_preds)^2
 
# Summary comparison table
comparison <- tibble(
  Model    = c("HPI Baseline (linear)", "LASSO", "Random Forest", "XGBoost"),
  RMSE     = round(c(hpi_rmse, lasso_rmse, rf_rmse, xgb_rmse), 3),
  R_squared = round(c(hpi_r2, lasso_r2, rf_r2, xgb_r2), 3)
) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)
 
cat("\n=== MODEL COMPARISON ===\n")
print(comparison)
 
# Visual comparison
comparison %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(RMSE, R_squared), names_to = "metric") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Model, value), y = value, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Model Comparison — RMSE and R²",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. SHAP
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
shap <- shapviz(xgb_model, X_pred = xgb_test_x)

sv_importance(shap, kind = "beeswarm") +
  labs(title = "SHAP Beeswarrm - Feature Impact on Life Expectancy")

sv_importance(shap, kind = "bar") +
  labs(title = "SHAP Feature Importance (Mean |SHAP|)")

sv_dependence(shap, v = "percapitaincome") +
  labs(title = "SHAP Dependence - Per Capita Income")

sv_waterfall(shap, row_id = 1) +
  labs(title = "SHAP Waterfall - Single Tract Breakdown")
```
